social_circle.name: Denise Burley

demographics.occupation: Administrative coordinator at a medical office

background.how_they_met: Denise is Fredick's younger sister. They grew up together in Bedford-Stuyvesant with both parents in a strict but loving household.
background.why_close: She is his closest family member, his emergency keyholder, and the person he calls when he feels isolated or worried. She keeps him connected to family because she is more social than he is.

personality_mini_profile.communication_style: Warm and direct, usually texts in complete sentences with occasional affectionate shorthand. She checks in, asks practical questions, and follows up if Fredick sounds too quiet.

recent_text_topics: Coordinating their usual Sunday call and whether Fredick will come to Queens this month.
Checking on Denise's arthritis and Fredick's knee after pickleball.
Planning who is bringing what to an upcoming family birthday or summer cookout.
Denise reminding Fredick not to overdo it with dental bills, late invoices, and too much worrying.
social_circle.evidence_from_interview: Q05 says Fredick has a younger sister, Denise, who lives in Queens, and that they speak most Sundays. Q05 also says he relies on Denise most because she is more social and keeps him connected. Q12 says his sister has a spare key for emergencies. Q44 says he called Denise during a rough week because he needed a familiar voice.

social_circle.name: Tasha Burley

background.how_they_met: Tasha is Denise's daughter and Fredick's adult niece. Fredick has known her since birth and helped occasionally when she and Marcus were younger.
background.why_close: Tasha asks Fredick about family history and pushes him to think about younger people's experience with rent, debt, politics, and activism. Their bond is rooted in family memory, Brooklyn history, and intergenerational political conversation.

personality_mini_profile.communication_style: Fast texter who sends links, screenshots, and long thoughts in bursts. Uses some emojis and group-chat humor, and is more emotionally explicit than the older generation.

recent_text_topics: Asking Fredick for details about grandparents' migration from Georgia and South Carolina.
Sending him articles about rent, student debt, and older Brooklyn residents being priced out.
Pushing the family group chat about a local Black history exhibit or community event.
Light teasing about Fredick over-researching his Kyoto trip instead of booking it.
social_circle.evidence_from_interview: Q06 identifies Tasha as Denise's daughter and one of Fredick's closest immediate family members. Q06 says Tasha asks more about family history. Q25 says Tasha especially pushes Fredick to see how debt and rent shape her generation. Q30 says Tasha was more activist, posted a lot online, and pushes the family group chat.

social_circle.name: Marcus Burley

demographics.occupation: Assistant manager at a logistics and retail supply company

background.how_they_met: Marcus is Denise's son and Fredick's adult nephew. Fredick has known him since childhood and sometimes helped with pickups or watching Denise's children when they were young.
background.why_close: Marcus sees Fredick as a steady older male relative who understands work, scheduling, management pressure, and the importance of getting promises in writing.

personality_mini_profile.communication_style: Short, practical texts. He often opens with a quick question, sends screenshots of work issues, and prefers direct advice over long emotional conversation.

recent_text_topics: Asking Fredick how to handle a difficult scheduling conflict at work.
Checking whether Fredick is watching a Knicks or Yankees game.
Coordinating attendance for Denise's next family gathering.
Talking about how rising rent and job stability are affecting younger workers.
social_circle.evidence_from_interview: Q06 identifies Marcus as Denise's son and one of Fredick's closest immediate family members. Q06 says Marcus sometimes comes to Fredick for work advice. Q19 says Fredick sometimes helped with nieces and nephews when they were young. Q30 says Denise worried about Marcus during the increased focus on race and policing.

social_circle.name: Calvin Price

background.how_they_met: Calvin and Fredick met through retail work many years ago. Calvin is an old coworker who remained a personal friend after Fredick moved from full-time operations management into consulting.
background.why_close: They share long experience in Brooklyn retail, a practical temperament, and a quiet way of discussing politics, aging, work, and neighborhood change without turning everything into an argument.

personality_mini_profile.communication_style: Brief and conversational, with dry jokes and occasional all-caps emphasis. He texts to confirm plans, send a sports comment, or check in without making a big emotional display.

shared_activities: checking in about health and retirement
watching or texting about New York sports
recent_text_topics: Confirming their every-other-Friday diner coffee on 18th Avenue.
Trading comments about the Knicks and Yankees.
Talking about late invoices, retirement timing, and whether consulting is worth the stress.
Quiet discussion about policing, race, and younger workers without wanting social media arguments.
social_circle.evidence_from_interview: Q07 names Calvin as an old coworker who meets Fredick for coffee every other Friday. Q07 says they meet at a diner on 18th Avenue. Q27 says Fredick talks about race and policing with older friends quietly. Q30 says Calvin is close to Fredick: concerned, thoughtful, and not interested in shouting matches.

social_circle.name: Ruth Stein

background.how_they_met: Ruth met Fredick through a photography class. Their friendship grew through gallery openings, photo walks, and shared interest in local exhibits.
background.why_close: Ruth connects with Fredick's reflective side: photography, museums, Black-and-white street scenes, local history, and noticing quiet city corners. She is one of the few non-family friends who actively pulls him into cultural outings.

personality_mini_profile.communication_style: Texts in polished full sentences, often with links to exhibit pages or a quick critique of a photo. She may send a few photos at once and expects thoughtful replies.

recent_text_topics: Sending Fredick a notice for a local photography exhibit worth seeing.
Commenting on one of his black-and-white street photos and suggesting a tighter crop.
Planning a monthly gallery opening or photo walk.
Encouraging him to print a few photos instead of only posting them online.
social_circle.evidence_from_interview: Q07 names Ruth as a woman from Fredick's photography class who tells him when a local exhibit is worth seeing. Q07 says he sees Ruth maybe once a month at a gallery opening or photo walk. Q48 says Fredick posts a black-and-white street photo every few weeks and follows photography, jazz, and museum pages.
